scenarios.name: carbon_roof_on_wagon
scenarios.change: MY27.1 carbon roof released for wagon
rules_added: R3 only on S1, C1, W1

impact.change: MY27.1 carbon roof released for wagon

impact_locked.change: MY27.1 carbon roof released for wagon

scenarios.briefing: The MY27.1 release widens the carbon roof (R3) rule from "only on S1, C1" to "only on S1, C1, W1," which opens the carbon roof to the wagon and raises buildable configurations from 1644 to 1722 (78 added, 0 removed). Because the change only adds possibilities, no planned configuration becomes invalid (0 configs, 0 cars), so the free replan and the locked replan give identical results. Both keep all 600 orders, replace none, move no cars to a different day and resequence none, so there are 0 supplier call-off changes. The plan does not use any of the new wagon carbon roof configurations: carbon roof volume stays at 50 cars, configurations used stay at 107, and the mix gap stays at 140, so the release neither blocks anything nor improves the mix by itself. We recommend releasing the rule change into the current plan as-is and adding wagon carbon roof demand to the target mix in the next weekly planning round, if sales has orders for it, so the 78 new configurations can start working on the gap of 140.

scenarios.name: new_highway_pilot
scenarios.change: MY27.1 highway pilot A2 launched (electric only, EU+US)
rules_added: US cars must carry A1 or A2

impact.change: MY27.1 highway pilot A2 launched (electric only, EU+US)

impact_locked.change: MY27.1 highway pilot A2 launched (electric only, EU+US)

scenarios.briefing: The launch of the highway pilot (A2) on electric cars (P3) in the EU and US raises buildable configurations from 1644 to 1860, with 216 added and none removed. US cars may now carry either the driver assistance pack (A1) or A2. No configuration or car in the current plan becomes invalid, so nothing is forced and all 600 orders could legally stay as they are. The free replan uses the new option anyway: it replaces 61 orders, keeps 539, and puts A2 on 60 cars while A1 drops from 419 to 359. It also widens the configurations in use from 107 to 119 and resequences 2 kept cars without moving any car to another day, for 63 supplier call-off changes and a mix gap of 184 (from 140 before). The locked plan changes nothing and causes 0 call-off changes, but its mix gap grows to 304 because it builds no A2 at all, and A2 is capped by its rules to electric cars, which stay at 200, in EU and US markets only. I recommend the free replan, since 63 call-off changes buy a gap of 184 instead of 304, provided the highway pilot supplier can confirm the 60 units and the A1 supplier accepts the reduction to 359.

scenarios.name: sport_seats_need_sport_trim
scenarios.change: MY27.1 sport seats now only with sport trim

impact.change: MY27.1 sport seats now only with sport trim

impact_locked.change: MY27.1 sport seats now only with sport trim

scenarios.briefing: For MY27.1, sport seats (S2) may now only be combined with sport trim (T2) instead of sport trim or premium trim (T3), which cuts buildable configurations from 1644 to 1456 (188 removed, none added). This invalidates 11 configurations in the current plan covering 72 cars, all because of the new rule "S2 requires T2." The free replan replaces 142 orders and keeps 458, holding the mix gap at 140 by spreading the plan from 107 to 128 configurations, at a cost of 142 call-off changes. The locked replan replaces only the 72 invalid cars and keeps 528 orders, which means 72 call-off changes, but the mix gap doubles from 140 to 280 because it stays on the same 107 configurations. Neither version is blocked by slot or sequence capacity, since no kept car moves day or gets resequenced, and in the plan sport seats stay at 167 while sport trim rises from 198 to 200 and premium trim falls from 193 to 191. I recommend taking the locked replan now to keep supplier call-off changes to 72, then working down the 280 gap in the next weekly mix cycle rather than paying 70 extra call-off changes immediately.
